o: We build target left to right; dp[i] = minimum cost to have constructed target[:i]. From each reachable position i, every word that matches target at position i offers a transition to i + len(word) with its cost. With ≤ 50 words and target length ≤ 2000, the direct check is at most 50·2000·2000 character comparisons — acceptable in compiled languages and fine in practice.
k: This is a shortest-path / knapsack-style DP over prefix positions of target.
dp[i] considers all words matching target[i:i+len(w)]; answer is dp[L] or -1.
Matching can be accelerated by grouping words by length or first letter, but the naive check fits the constraints.

a.n: Approach 1: Prefix-position DP with direct matching
a.i: Process positions left to right; for each position with finite dp, try appending every word whose characters match target starting there, relaxing dp[i+len(word)].
s: For i in 0..L-1 with dp[i] < INF: for each (word, cost): if target starts with word at i, dp[i+len] = min(dp[i+len], dp[i]+cost).
a.t: O(L·Σ|word|) ≈ 2e8 worst case in C++/Java, fine; Python may need the grouped optimization below

a.n: Approach 2: Deduplicate words and group by length
a.i: Duplicate words waste time; keep the minimum cost per distinct word. Additionally, bucket words by length so each position only attempts words of feasible remaining length — a constant-factor win that matters in Python.
s: Group distinct words by length into lists.
DP as before, iterating length buckets present at position i.
a.t: O(L·D·avgLen) with D distinct words ≤ 50 — same asymptotics, smaller constants

w: State the DP clearly: positions are nodes, word appends are edges with weights, and we want the shortest path 0 → L (a DAG, so simple relaxation in order works). Pitfalls: unreachable positions must be skipped (or guarded against INF overflow), and returning -1 when dp[L] stays infinite. Follow-up: the Hard version lifts word count to 5e4, requiring Aho–Corasick or grouping by (length, first chars) with per-length rolling minima.
